correctness.rationale: The no-jump dissipation identity excludes every undamped non-Hermitian eigenstate except Hermitian eigenvectors annihilated by the entire collision detector. In the two-boson symmetric basis, the leaf-doublon equations force all hub-leaf amplitudes to vanish, pair equations force zero energy, and the remaining hub-leaf equations are exactly Bc=0. Full row rank follows from any triple of leaves, yielding the entire projector and sharp dimension. Exact rational observability checks on 13 cases and independent incidence-projector identities corroborate but do not replace the all-q proof.

originality.rationale: The precise weighted two-boson star collision-loss projector, q=4 onset, and pairwise arbitrary-hopping capture law were not present or implied as evaluated statements in inspected primary studies of dark quantum walks, bosonic two-body walks, non-Hermitian lattice correlations, or one-excitation star trapping. Closest cyclic-collision studies concern nonisomorphic single-particle graphs and different spectral eigenspaces. This is a best-knowledge comparison with meaningful residual priority risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier doublon-decay or collision-monitoring star calculation could contain an equivalent result.
The full text of Pouthier (2022) could not be examined, although its accessible abstract concerns attractive coherent binding rather than the specified collision-loss model.
Broad general spectral-control results may admit a non-obvious reduction to this exact formula; no such dominating explicit implication was found in the inspected material.

value.rationale: A physically natural pair-loss channel has a sharp, universal degree-four interference threshold and a full capture functional for all positive star couplings and all unequal positive detection rates. Uniform-star survival tends to one for initially separated leaf pairs as degree grows, a substantive topology-driven protection law beyond a routine bound or one isolated finite calculation.
